test.name: Census born-minus-living names a deceased child that is a research target
test.description: Re-authored from the retired ut_init_project_q4v now that gap analysis is question-selection's job, not init-project's. From 1900/1910 census fertility counts given in the delegation, the skill must call census_children_gap and find TWO missing children: one born and died before the June 1900 enumeration (children-born minus children-living), and one living child born between the two censuses. The failure this guards: reading living-count parity with the tree as 'accounted for' and never making the pre-1900 deceased child a research target.

input.delegation:
Select and record the next research question for this project.

The 1900 US census records 6 children born to Margaret Mercer and 5 still living. The 1910 US census records 8 children born and 7 still living.

projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: Should call census_children_gap with motherId I1, projectPath, and both census entries (1900: 6 born/5 living; 1910: 8 born/7 living) before writing a question

The tool reports TWO missing children: one died before the 1900 enumeration (born on or before 1900-06-01), and one living child born between the 1900 and 1910 enumerations. Grade the written question and the reply together against this, not against one child alone
The pre-1900 deceased child is absent from the tree; the five tree children born before 1900 (Mary, John, Anna, Edward, Grace) are the survivors, not proof the family is complete
The post-1900 living child is NOT William Mercer (already in the tree, b. 1906) — it is a child the tree does not yet have

Only one question may be open at a time, so the written question may target one of the two children. The reply must still name the other as a remaining research target. A reply that never mentions the pre-1900 deceased child is a FAIL on the gap dimension, not a partial
The deceased child is a research target (born and died before the enumeration), not a tree or data error — do not present it as a person_warnings-style contradiction
The question's selection_basis should be objective_decomposition (Priority 3 — a missing-child group from census_children_gap), per the skill's priority table
